dslr-camera.definition: A digital single-lens reflex camera that uses a mirror system and an optical viewfinder.
dslr-camera.exampleUsage: The photographer mounted a lens on the DSLR camera.

mirrorless-camera.definition: A digital interchangeable-lens camera that does not use the reflex mirror found in a DSLR.
mirrorless-camera.exampleUsage: The mirrorless camera displayed the scene electronically.

lens.definition: An optical camera component focusing light to form an image.

wide-angle-lens.definition: A camera lens that captures a wide view of a scene.

telephoto-lens.definition: A camera lens that produces a larger image of a distant subject.

tripod.definition: A three-legged stand that keeps a camera steady.

monopod.definition: A single-legged camera support used to add stability while remaining easier to move than a tripod.
monopod.exampleUsage: The photographer supported the long lens with a monopod.

camera-strap.definition: A strap attached to a camera so it can be carried more securely.
camera-strap.exampleUsage: The camera strap was secured before the shoot.

lens-cap.definition: A removable cover protecting an unused camera lens.
lens-cap.exampleUsage: Omar puts the lens cap on the unused lens.

camera-bag.definition: A padded bag designed to protect and organize cameras, lenses, and accessories.
camera-bag.exampleUsage: The lenses were stored in the camera bag.

flash.definition: A light that briefly shines to illuminate a photograph.

softbox.definition: A light modifier with translucent material that spreads and softens light from a lamp or flash.
softbox.exampleUsage: The softbox produced broad soft light on the subject.

umbrella-light.definition: A photographic lighting setup that uses a reflective or translucent umbrella to spread and soften light.
umbrella-light.exampleUsage: The umbrella light created a wider light source.

ring-light.definition: A circular light designed to illuminate a subject from around the camera or lens axis.
ring-light.exampleUsage: The ring light provided even frontal illumination.

reflector.definition: A surface that bounces light onto the subject of a photograph.

diffuser.definition: A translucent material or device spreading light in photography.
diffuser.exampleUsage: The diffuser spreads light over the subject.

light-stand.definition: An adjustable stand designed to support photographic lights or modifiers.
light-stand.exampleUsage: The light stand was weighted and placed away from the walkway.

continuous-light.definition: A photographic light source that stays on continuously instead of flashing only at exposure.
continuous-light.exampleUsage: The continuous light let the photographer preview the shadows.

strobe.definition: A photographic light producing a brief flash for image capture.
strobe.exampleUsage: The strobe produces a brief flash.

gel-filter.definition: A thin colored or corrective sheet placed over a light to change its color or spectral output.
gel-filter.exampleUsage: A blue gel filter changed the background-light color.

backdrop.definition: A background placed behind a subject or scene.

background-paper.definition: A wide roll or sheet of paper used as a seamless photographic backdrop.
background-paper.exampleUsage: The product was placed in front of white background paper.

posing-stool.definition: A stool used to seat or support a subject during a portrait session.
posing-stool.exampleUsage: The subject sat on the posing stool.

props-table.definition: A table used to organize objects and accessories needed for a photo session.
props-table.exampleUsage: Small props were arranged on the props table.

makeup-station.definition: A dedicated area with a mirror, lighting, and surface for preparing makeup or grooming before a shoot.
makeup-station.exampleUsage: The model prepared at the makeup station.

wardrobe-rack.definition: A rail or rack used to hang clothing for a photo session.
wardrobe-rack.exampleUsage: The outfits were organized on the wardrobe rack.

clamp.definition: A fastening device holding suitable equipment or material in place.

sandbag.definition: A heavy bag of sand used to hold photographic equipment steady.

gaffer-tape.definition: A strong cloth-backed pressure-sensitive tape used in film, photography, and stage work for temporary securing and labeling.
gaffer-tape.exampleUsage: The crew used gaffer tape to secure a cable cover.

extension-cord.definition: A flexible cable that carries electricity from an outlet to a device farther away.
extension-cord.exampleUsage: The extension cord remains away from the walkway.

shutter-button.definition: The camera control that triggers an exposure and takes a photograph.
shutter-button.exampleUsage: The photographer pressed the shutter button.

viewfinder.definition: An optical or electronic viewing device used to compose a photograph.
viewfinder.exampleUsage: Maya composes the image through the viewfinder.

lcd-screen.definition: A liquid-crystal display on a camera used to show settings, menus, or captured images.
lcd-screen.exampleUsage: The photographer reviewed the image on the LCD screen.

memory-card.definition: A small removable digital storage device used to save photos, video, or other data.
memory-card.exampleUsage: The camera saved the files to a memory card.

battery.definition: A device storing energy and supplying electrical power to a camera.
battery.exampleUsage: The battery supplies power to the camera.

hot-shoe.definition: A mounting point on top of many cameras that can hold and electrically connect compatible accessories such as a flash.
hot-shoe.exampleUsage: The flash was attached to the camera's hot shoe.

dial.definition: A rotating control used to change a camera setting.

focus-ring.definition: A rotating ring on a camera lens used to adjust focus manually.
focus-ring.exampleUsage: The photographer turned the focus ring while checking sharpness.

image-sensor.definition: The light-sensitive electronic component in a digital camera that converts incoming light into image data.
image-sensor.exampleUsage: The image sensor sits behind the lens mount.

lens-hood.definition: An attachment helping shield a lens from unwanted stray light.
lens-hood.exampleUsage: The lens hood helps block unwanted stray light.

computer-monitor.definition: A screen displaying information or images from a computer.
computer-monitor.exampleUsage: Omar reviews the image on the computer monitor.

editing-software.definition: Computer software used to organize, adjust, retouch, or process photographs and other images.
editing-software.exampleUsage: The photographer adjusted exposure in editing software.

color-wheel.definition: A circular representation of relationships among colors.

histogram.definition: A chart showing the distribution of image values, such as brightness levels.

crop-tool.definition: An editing tool used to remove outer parts of an image and change its framing or aspect ratio.
crop-tool.exampleUsage: The crop tool tightened the composition.

brush-tool.definition: An editing tool that applies adjustments, paint, masks, or effects to selected image areas.
brush-tool.exampleUsage: The editor used the brush tool for a local adjustment.

layer.definition: A separate level of a digital image that can be edited on its own.

filter.definition: An image-effect or adjustment tool in this editing context.
filter.exampleUsage: The editor applies a black-and-white filter.

preset.definition: A saved group of camera or editing settings.

export.definition: To save a finished project in a chosen file format.

portrait.definition: A photograph of a person, usually showing their face.

landscape.definition: A picture showing natural scenery such as hills or fields.

macro.definition: Photography that shows small subjects in close detail.
macro.exampleUsage: Macro photography shows the small object in close detail.

product-shot.definition: A photograph made to present a product clearly, often for advertising, catalogs, or online stores.
product-shot.exampleUsage: The product shot showed the item against a clean background.

fashion.definition: Clothing or style as the subject of photography in this lesson.
fashion.exampleUsage: The fashion photograph presents the agreed clothing.

wedding.definition: The social event at which the ceremony of marriage is performed.

event.definition: An organized occasion being photographed in this context.
event.exampleUsage: The photographer covers an adult community event.

food-photography.definition: Photography focused on presenting food and drinks in an appealing or informative way.
food-photography.exampleUsage: The studio specializes in food photography for menus.

black-and-white.definition: Describing an image made mainly from shades of gray rather than full color.
black-and-white.exampleUsage: The portrait was converted to black and white.

panorama.definition: A picture (or series of pictures) representing a continuous scene.

camera.definition: A device recording photographs digitally or on film.

light-box.definition: A small illuminated enclosure or translucent setup used to create even light around objects, especially for product photography.
light-box.exampleUsage: The jewelry was photographed inside a light box.

aperture.definition: The opening in a lens through which light enters the camera.
aperture.exampleUsage: The aperture is the opening through which light enters.

shutter-speed.definition: The length of time a camera's shutter or electronic exposure remains open to record light.
shutter-speed.exampleUsage: A faster shutter speed reduced motion blur.

iso.definition: A camera setting that affects image brightness and noise.

focus.definition: The adjustment determining which subject distance appears sharp.

exposure.definition: The light recorded by the sensor or film during image capture.

white-balance.definition: A camera or editing setting that adjusts colors so neutral objects appear neutral under different light sources.
white-balance.exampleUsage: The photographer adjusted white balance for the indoor lighting.

zoom.definition: To change the view or magnification; optical zoom changes lens focal length, while digital zoom uses cropping or processing.

wide-angle.definition: Describing a lens or view with a relatively broad field of view.
wide-angle.exampleUsage: A wide-angle lens captured more of the room.

edit.definition: To change or adjust an image using appropriate tools.

crop.definition: To remove the outer parts of an image.

retouch.definition: To edit a photograph to improve or change its appearance.

print.definition: To produce words or images on paper using a machine.
print.exampleUsage: Maya prints the agreed image on paper.

frame.definition: A holder or border around a photograph in this context.
frame.exampleUsage: A frame borders the finished print.

portfolio.definition: A selected collection showing a photographer’s work.
portfolio.exampleUsage: Maya selects six photographs for her portfolio.

gallery.definition: A collection or display of photographs.
